## What is a Jigsaw?

Jigsaw is a cooperative learning technique where you become an **expert** on one topic and then **teach** your peers. Research shows that teaching others is one of the most effective ways to learn.

In HPM 883, we use jigsaws to explore how methods from each unit are applied in real research. You'll read an application paper, analyze it with fellow experts, then teach what you learned to classmates who read different papers.

## How It Works

### Before Class

1. Check your **paper assignment** (posted 1 week before)
2. Read your assigned paper carefully
3. Complete the **reading guide** questions

### In Class (75 minutes)

::: {.callout-note}
## Phase 1: Expert Groups (20-25 min)
Meet with classmates assigned the **same paper**. Work through the analysis template together. Reach consensus on key points.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Phase 2: Teaching Groups (25-30 min)
Reshuffle into new groups where each member read a **different paper**. Teach your paper to your group (5-7 min each). Discuss patterns across papers.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Phase 3: Synthesis (15-20 min)
Whole-class discussion. Instructor highlights key insights and connects back to course concepts.
:::

Jigsaws are worth **20% of your final grade** (5 sessions × 40 points each, scaled). You may drop your **2 lowest** scores.

See the [detailed rubric](jigsaw-instructions.qmd#grading) for evaluation criteria.
